note: make check: All gates passed, measured by the orchestrator re-running it rather than quoted from a build report. 1424 passed, 0 SKIPPED, 0 failed - counted from the raw progress output (1424 characters, all dots) rather than the summary line. The zero skip count is the load-bearing figure: tests/conftest.py skips the whole integration suite at module level without Docker, so a green run with skips would prove nothing about the privacy boundary, the migrations or the RLS probes. Money module 100.00% branch, backend 92.54% line against an 80% floor, Kotlin 60.34% against a 60.39% committed floor, ruff and mypy clean across 116 source files. 94 new test functions across 8 files. SIX plan corrections, and the first two were the orchestrator's errors rather than the build's: (1) a stale 'Exactly five' claim carried out of team.md:659 into two planning documents WITHOUT opening the file - it reads 'Exactly eight' and was fixed in eec0f92 before D6 began, so the project's own rule about comments stating uncheckable numbers applied to the documents that state the rule; (2) the plan said the cascade assertion drops to ZERO after 0007 when nine retained tables remain reachable via owner -> batch, contradicting this unit's OWN nfr-design which established that is why BR1.6's refusal is load-bearing; (3) the manifest cannot express WHICH rows belong to an account, so the phone-scoped tables are reached by no constraint; (4) the two-path comparison is vacuous as written; (5) 'no new PUBLIC_ROUTES entry' forced a two-step route shape and a fourth lens exemption; (6) the regenerate-and-compare gate would NOT have caught a basis change, which is exactly what NFR14.101 is about. The build also caught a false disclosure in its OWN first output: LIFE_OF_ACCOUNT rendered as 'until the account is deleted' against the RETAIN_WITH_BASIS rows, which by definition SURVIVE deletion - the opposite of the truth on the exact point ADR-012 exists to disclose. Status counts, derived from the rows: 59 OK, 1 Deferred, zero GAP. The single Deferred row is NFR14.90, partly automated by design and not pretended otherwise.
